_note: The parameter catalogue for this corpus: every number a statute did not state, with its unit (the corpus's own units are accepted and scaled by the decoder), the convention its value comes from and its source. It starts empty: the plan decides which parameters exist and proposes each with a provisional value, and the harness enters the proposal here marked `proposed` (run, iteration, node) until the operator reviews it by removing the marker or changing the value; the doctor lists every unreviewed proposal. The operator-authored list this file carried before any law was planned is kept, out of the pipeline's path, under readings/legacy/. Figures the law states are literals on the rule's span, never entries here.

params.name: p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph
params.convention: The sampling period of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard, 20 Hz (one scene every 50 ms): the step bound of headingSince, the largest gap between two consecutive scenes it integrates across; not a look-back window and not an action window.

params.name: p.speed_resolution
params.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest speed the acquisition standard separates from standstill; a speed at or below it counts as no motion.
params.source: Ground-truth simulator kinematics sampled at 20 Hz and the speed noise of typical odometry

params.name: p.circulation_sine_tolerance
params.convention: Direction tolerance: the sine of the largest angle off a radial line within which motion about a point counts as neither sense of rotation, covering heading and position noise on entry and exit paths.
params.source: Measurement tolerance of velocity direction in ground-truth simulation

params.name: p.yaw_rate_resolution
params.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest yaw rate the acquisition standard separates from a straight path; a yaw rate at or below it counts as no heading change.
params.source: Yaw-rate noise of ground-truth simulator kinematics and of automotive inertial sensors

params.name: p.entering_combination_length
params.convention: Design-vehicle length: the overall length of the longest combination of vehicles a highway is designed to carry, standing for 'any other vehicle or combination of vehicles' that may enter the space.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book design vehicles (WB-67 interstate semitrailer, 73.5 ft)

params.name: p.entry_time_headway
params.convention: Safe time headway: the time gap kept to the vehicle ahead, applied once ahead of and once behind the entering vehicle at the subject's speed.
params.source: Two-second following rule of driver manuals and headway-based car-following conventions

params.name: p.same_direction_cosine
params.convention: Heading alignment tolerance: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings that still counts as travelling the same way.
params.source: Measurement tolerance of heading in ground-truth simulation and lane-keeping heading variation

params.name: p.overtaking_speed_margin
params.convention: Speed resolution of a speed difference: the smallest excess of the subject's speed over the other's that counts as gaining on it rather than keeping pace.
params.source: Speed noise of ground-truth simulator kinematics, doubled for a difference of two readings

params.name: p.turn_recognition_angle
params.convention: Turn recognition: the heading change through an intersection beyond which a passage counts as a turn rather than a straight crossing; half the right angle of a turn at a right-angled junction, leaving room for skewed junctions and lane offsets.
params.source: Intersection geometry conventions (AASHTO Green Book turning paths) and manoeuvre classification in trajectory datasets

params.name: p.opposed_direction_cosine
params.convention: Direction tolerance: minus the cosine of the narrowest angle between a velocity and a carrier's designated direction that counts as travel against it; motion at a smaller angle, crossing included, does not.
params.source: Wrong-way detection conventions in trajectory analysis and heading tolerance of ground-truth simulation

params.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
params.convention: Stop-point tolerance: the largest ground distance between a halted body and the line, crossing or intersection edge at which the halt counts as made at that place; a body farther upstream is outside the stopping zone.
params.source: MUTCD 2009 section 3B.16 stop-line placement (at least 4 ft ahead of the crosswalk) and vehicle positioning variability at a stop

params.name: p.intersection_sight_distance
params.convention: Intersection sight distance: the length of the crossing way, in the smaller of its two directions, that a driver halted on a stop-controlled approach must be able to see to judge a gap in approaching traffic.
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (2018) section 9.5.3, case B departure sight triangles at a low urban design speed

params.name: p.immediate_hazard_gap
params.convention: Critical gap: the time within which another road user's arrival at the conflict area, or its predicted closest approach, counts as an immediate hazard to a road user about to cross or join its path.
params.source: HCM 7th ed. Exhibit 20-11 base critical headway (major-street left turn)

params.name: p.conflict_clearance
params.convention: Conflict radius: the centre distance at predicted closest approach below which two road users' paths count as in conflict; about the half-length plus half-width of two passenger cars.
params.source: FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model (Gettman et al. 2008) conflict definition

params.name: p.opposed_carriers_cosine
params.convention: Direction tolerance: minus the cosine of the narrowest angle between two carriers' designated directions that counts as opposite directions; carriers within about 45 degrees of exactly opposed count.
params.source: Junction geometry: approaches meeting at an intersection skewed by up to 45 degrees (AASHTO Green Book ch. 9)

params.name: p.deceleration_resolution
params.convention: Sensor resolution: the smallest longitudinal deceleration the acquisition standard separates from steady speed; a deceleration at or below it counts as no slowing.
params.source: carla_scene_graph acquisition standard: acceleration resolution of the recorded kinematics

params.name: p.merge_time_headway
params.convention: Safe merge headway: the time an approaching vehicle on the highway would take, at its own speed, to close the gap to a vehicle entering or leaving the highway; a smaller gap is not reasonable safety.
params.source: Two-second following rule; HCM freeway merge gap acceptance

params.name: p.obstruction_encounter_reach
params.convention: Encounter reach: the ground distance from a pedestrian's body to an obstruction within which the pedestrian has come up against it.
params.source: HCM pedestrian body ellipse and shy distance to fixed objects

params.name: p.pedestrian_detour_offset
params.convention: Pedestrian detour width: the largest distance from the sidewalk at which a pedestrian walking on the adjacent highway counts as keeping to the side nearest the sidewalk; one pedestrian design width plus shy distance.
params.source: HCM pedestrian space (body ellipse about 0.6 m by 0.5 m) plus shy distance

params.name: p.sidewalk_return_time
params.convention: Return time: the time after a pedestrian has passed an obstruction within which a return to the sidewalk counts as made as soon as practicable; a few walking steps at the design walking speed.
params.source: HCM design walking speed (1.2 m/s)

params.name: p.access_crossing_reach
params.convention: Access reach: the ground distance from a vehicle's body to a driveway or alley entrance within which its presence in a bicycle lane counts as part of entering or exiting it; about one passenger-car length.
params.source: AASHTO design passenger car (P) length 5.8 m

params.name: p.passing_lateral_clearance
params.convention: Passing clearance: the smallest surface gap between a cycle or scooter and a motor vehicle it passes alongside at which the pass endangers neither the rider nor the vehicle's occupants; the three-foot passing-clearance convention applied from the rider's side.
params.source: three-foot passing-clearance statutes and AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities

params.name: p.u_turn_window
params.convention: U-turn recognition window: the longest time over which a reversal of heading, made in one movement or in several forward and backing movements, is recognized as one turning; a multi-point turn on a narrow street.
params.source: observed durations of three-point turns (naturalistic driving studies)

params.name: p.u_turn_reversal_tolerance
params.convention: Reversal tolerance: the largest difference between the size of the heading change over the window and a half turn within which the road user counts as proceeding in the opposite direction; covers the offset of a turn into a lane of the opposite direction and heading noise.
params.source: trajectory-classification practice for U-turn detection

params.name: p.child_presence_reach
params.convention: Presence reach: the ground distance from a child's body to a travel region of a school zone within which the child counts as present in the zone; the width of a sidewalk and verge beside the roadway.
params.source: urban street cross-section conventions (sidewalk and buffer widths)

params.name: p.turn_approach_length
params.convention: Turn approach: the distance travelled just before entering an intersection over which a turning vehicle's approach is judged; about two passenger-car lengths, shorter than the storage of a short turn bay.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book turn-lane storage practice

params.name: p.course_departure_sine
params.convention: Course-departure tolerance: the sine of the angle between a road user's velocity and its carrier's designated direction beyond which it counts as leaving its direct course rather than tracking the carrier; about three degrees, above heading noise and lane-keeping drift.
params.source: lane-change onset detection practice in naturalistic driving studies

params.name: p.offroad_stop_reach
params.convention: Off-road stopping reach: the ground distance from a halted vehicle's body to a shoulder within which moving off the main-traveled part counts as practicable; about one lane width of lateral movement.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book lane and shoulder widths

params.name: p.stopping_conflict_gap
params.convention: Conflict standoff: the largest surface gap from a halted road user's body to another road user ahead of it at which the halt counts as necessary to avoid a conflict; a queue spacing at standstill.
params.source: queue spacing at standstill (traffic-flow jam-density conventions)

params.name: p.free_passage_width
params.convention: Free-passage width: the smallest width of an unoccupied lane beside a standing vehicle that lets another vehicle pass; a design passenger-car width plus lateral clearance.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book design-vehicle widths and lane widths

params.name: p.opposite_lane_reach
params.convention: Beside reach: the largest ground distance from a standing vehicle's body to a lane within which the lane counts as opposite the vehicle; covers the lateral gap between the body and the next lane's edge.
params.source: lane-keeping offset conventions

params.name: p.perception_reaction_time
params.convention: Perception-reaction time: the time a driver keeps its speed before braking begins, in the stopping sight distance model.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance (brake reaction time)

params.name: p.braking_decel_dry
params.convention: Braking deceleration on a dry surface: a firm, controlled stop most drivers make on dry pavement.
params.source: stopping-distance studies of driver braking on dry pavement (about 0.45 g)

params.name: p.braking_decel_wet
params.convention: Design braking deceleration: the deceleration most drivers keep within their lane and control on a wet surface, used by the stopping sight distance model.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance (deceleration rate)

params.name: p.braking_decel_ice
params.convention: Braking deceleration on an icy or snow-covered surface: the deceleration packed snow or ice allows under controlled braking.
params.source: winter-road friction measurements (friction coefficient about 0.15)

params.name: p.curve_lateral_accel
params.convention: Curve lateral acceleration: the lateral acceleration (speed squared times curvature) above which a curve is taken faster than ordinary drivers' comfort and control margin.
params.source: side-friction and driver-comfort studies of curve negotiation

params.name: p.lateral_margin_time
params.convention: Speed-proportional lateral margin: the lateral room beside a vehicle, both sides together, that grows with speed to absorb lateral wander; the speed times this time must fit in the lane width beyond the vehicle's width.
params.source: lane-width and lateral-clearance studies of speed choice

params.name: p.traffic_time_headway
params.convention: Minimum time headway in traffic: the time gap to the road user ahead in the lane below which the speed is too high for the traffic.
params.source: car-following headway conventions

params.name: p.oncoming_heading_cosine
params.convention: Oncoming tolerance: the cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed headings within which two road users count as oncoming; about 45 degrees, covering bends and lane offsets on a two-way road.
params.source: heading-alignment tolerance of the acquisition standard

params.name: p.low_beam_reveal_distance
params.convention: Low-beam reveal distance: the distance ahead to which the lowermost distribution of light reveals persons and vehicles, as the multiple-beam equipment standard sets it for the lowermost beam.
params.source: NRS 484D.210(2), lowermost beam reveal distance (100 feet)

declarations.meaning: The place of the observation lies inside the territorial limits of an incorporated city, as declared for the map or the trace.
The place of the observation lies outside every business district declared for the map or the trace.
The source's current plan for the road user includes a left turn at the target region.
The calendar day of the observation is one on which the school the zone serves is not in session, as declared for the map or the trace.

The time of the observation lies at least a half hour after the school the zone serves last ceased operation and at least a half hour before it next begins operation, as declared for the map or the trace.
The time of the observation lies within the hours during which the pupils of the school the zone serves are in class, as declared for the map or the trace.
The source's current plan for the road user includes a turn, to either hand, at the target region.
The place of the observation lies inside a business district or a residence district declared for the map or the trace.

_fields.aggregates: optional operator overrides only: word, classes (ru.* ids or other words). The run derives every aggregate the laws use from the corpus definitions (results/<run>/reading.json, for review); an operator entry here takes precedence over the derived one.
